draft.title: Renting
card: In NSW, the Residential Tenancies Act 2010 sets out the rights and duties of landlords and tenants. A written agreement between them is called a residential tenancy agreement.
Money a tenant pays at the start as security. In NSW it is held by a government body, not by the landlord, and it can be used to cover unpaid rent or damage beyond fair wear and tear.
The landlord must keep the home in a reasonable state of repair and fit to live in. The tenant must keep it reasonably clean and not damage it.

A landlord cannot simply make a tenant leave. The Act sets minimum notice periods, and if a tenant stays on after a valid notice, the landlord must apply to the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT) for an order.
draft.remember: The Act gives landlords and tenants each duties, and disputes are settled by rules, not by force.

a.q: Which statement about a rental bond in NSW is correct?
opts: Security money held by a government body during the tenancy
Security money kept by the landlord to spend as they like
A non-refundable fee paid to the landlord to start the lease
The first month of rent, paid in advance to the landlord
a.why: The bond is security for the landlord's losses, such as unpaid rent or damage, and a government body holds it. The tempting option that the landlord keeps it is wrong because the Act keeps the money out of the landlord's hands.
a.clue: Who holds the money while the tenancy lasts?

b.q: Tariq rents a unit in Parramatta. The oven stops working because it is old, and he did not misuse it. His landlord refuses to fix it and tells Tariq to leave. What is the correct legal position?
opts: The landlord must repair it and cannot just make him leave
The landlord need not repair it, but must give notice
Tariq must pay for the repair because he uses the oven
Tariq may leave at once and the landlord keeps the bond
b.why: The landlord has a duty to keep the home in a reasonable state of repair, and a worn oven is not the tenant's fault. A landlord cannot make a tenant leave without following the notice rules, so telling him to go does not end the tenancy. The option that only mentions notice is wrong because the repair duty still applies.
b.clue: Who owes the duty to repair, and does a landlord's say-so end a tenancy?

a.best: Security money held by a government body during the tenancy

b.best: The landlord must repair it and cannot just make him leave
